messages.text: Can Europe inspire new 'Medinah miracle' at Presidents Cup?

metadata.summary: If the International Team are going to end Team USA’s Presidents Cup dominance this week, live on Sky Sports, they may require their own 'Miracle at Medinah' to do it.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup 2026: Can Europe inspire new 'Miracle at Medinah' and shock International Team victory over Team USA? | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup 2026: Can Europe inspire new 'Miracle at Medinah' and shock International Team victory over Team USA? Team USA have won the last 10 editions of the Presidents Cup; Geoff Ogilvy captains the International Team as they look for a first victory on American soil; Ryan Fox revealed how the Internationals plan to take inspiration from Team Europe this week at Medinah, live on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Wednesday 23 September 2026 06:37, UK Image: Adam Scott, Ryan Fox, Hideki Matsuyama and Min Woo Lee all feature for the International Team at the Presidents Cup If the International Team are going to end Team USA’s Presidents Cup dominance this week, live on Sky Sports, they may require their own 'Miracle at Medinah' to do it. Fourteen years on from Team Europe producing a historic final-day comeback to claim Ryder Cup glory at the same venue, Geoff Ogilvy sees his side head in as heavy underdogs to avoid an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup defeat. The United States have won every edition since 2005 and only been beaten once in the event's history, before seven of the 24 players involved in this year's contest were even born, with all logic pointing to that run continuing in Illinois. Since winning the British Grand Prix at the start of July, their second win in the space of three races, Ferrari have seen their challenge in both championship battles fade with Charles Leclerc's second place in Belgium before the summer break their only podium finish from the last five rounds. metadata.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could be forced to undergo knee surgery that would end his season, according to ESPN.
metadata.content: NFL: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could be forced to undergo knee surgery that would end his season | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could be forced to undergo knee surgery that would end his season Jaxson Dart's injured left knee injury could force him out for the NFL season with New York Giants coach John Harbaugh saying the star quarterback is being evaluated in the aftermath of his side's defeat at the LA Rams on Monday night Wednesday 23 September 2026 06:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Week 2 game between New York Giants and Los Angeles Rams New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could be forced to undergo knee surgery that would end his season, according to ESPN. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Dart's injured left knee is being evaluated in the aftermath of the starting quarterback exiting the game in defeat at the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night . Dart was hurt less than four minutes into the game while being pressured on third-and-eight. Rams linebacker Byron Young hit Dart from the quarterback's right side, sending him into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who undercut Dart's legs, resulting in a heavy fall. metadata.content: Mikel Arteta contract: Arsenal boss agrees new deal to extend stay at Premier League champions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mikel Arteta contract: Arsenal boss agrees new deal to extend stay at Premier League champions Mikel Arteta has agreed to a new deal at Arsenal; Arteta had entered the final year of his current contract at the club but now extends his stay at the Emirates Stadium; the 44-year-old is already the longest-serving manager in England's top-four leagues after his appointment in 2019 Tuesday 22 September 2026 19:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol and Gary Cotterill provide the latest on Mikel Arteta's Arsenal future as he is expected to sign a new contract Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal to extend his stay at Arsenal. The 44-year-old's existing contract with the Premier League champions, signed in September 2024, was due to expire next summer. But the Spaniard, who was appointed in 2019, has committed his future to the club and confirmation of his new agreement is expected during this international break. When asked about his contract situation ahead of Arsenal's trip to Brighton on Saturday, Arteta said: "I think we are all very much aligned; whenever the time is right, we'll get that done.
